comments.body:
Background research (moved out of the description, unchanged). The description keeps the decision, the confirmed mechanism, the scope, the safety property, and the acceptance criteria; this is the prior art and options analysis that produced the recommendation.

## The problem (original framing)

Gerrit is the source of truth; GitHub is a read-only mirror. Gerrit's `Verified` label (CI per
patchset) is the real merge gate. GitHub Actions ALSO runs on `main` post-merge as a safety net.

When commits land close together the mirror's `main` runs get CANCELLED as superseded, so
GitHub shows a long trail of red X's on a `main` that is actually healthy.

Operator's framing: do NOT spend cycles validating every individual commit — Gerrit's
per-patchset gate is the protection. Main CI matters as a safety net, but the value is
"is main healthy NOW", not "was every commit green". Mirror what comparable projects do.

## What comparable projects actually do (VERIFIED via GitHub API)

| Mirror repo | Workflows | Check runs on latest main commit |
|---|---|---|
| golang/go | NONE (.github/workflows 404) | **0** |
| openstack/nova | NONE | **0** |
| LibreOffice/core | lockdown.yml only (issue-locking bot) | **0** |
| aosp-mirror/platform_frameworks_base | - | **0** |
| qt/qtbase | ninja-build.yml, `on: push` | outlier - see below |

**Four of five major Gerrit-primary projects surface NO per-commit CI on the GitHub mirror at
all.** The mirror is a code mirror, full stop. Qt is the exception and its answer is to make the
job cheap enough that cancellation never matters ("finish as fast as possible", system libs,
ccache) rather than to report per-commit truth.

Where their real post-merge signal lives:
- **Go** - post-submit on LUCI (ci.chromium.org/p/golang), dashboard at build.golang.org. Never GitHub.
- **OpenStack/Zuul** - the closest precedent to what the operator wants, and it is a FIRST-CLASS
  FEATURE, not a workaround. Zuul's `post` pipeline uses the **supercedent** manager, which
  collapses queued items per project-ref: "If more than one additional item is enqueued for the
  project-ref, previously enqueued items which have not started processing are removed." That is
  literally "test main's current state, not every commit". Separate `periodic` (daily 02:00 UTC),
  `periodic-weekly`, `periodic-stable` pipelines carry the health-over-time signal.
- **Kubernetes Prow/Tide** - batches PRs, tests the batch, merges together. Tide's docs describe
  NO post-merge branch testing; the model is entirely pre-merge.
- **Chromium/ChromeOS** - post-submit builders trigger every **7-10 hours**, deliberately covering
  many commits at once, with sheriffs watching. This is the direct answer to the bisect question.

## GitHub Actions mechanics (VERIFIED against docs)

- **Cancelled == red X cannot be fixed natively.** GitHub staff acknowledged it Dec 2021; still
  open in 2026 (community discussion 8336).
- **`cancel-in-progress: false` alone does NOT fix it.** With the default `queue: single`, an
  existing PENDING run in the group is cancelled and replaced - you still get a red X, just on a
  different run.
- **A workflow cannot decline to report.** Actions creates CHECK RUNS intrinsically; the
  `statuses:` permission governs only commit statuses pushed via API, so `statuses: none` does
  nothing.
- **The only "hide" path is deleting runs after the fact** (MercuryTechnologies/delete-cancelled-runs).
- **GitHub merge queue is structurally inapplicable** - `merge_group` is driven by PRs entering a
  queue; with Gerrit owning the merge decision there are no PRs and `main` advances by mirror push.

## Options (option 3 was chosen)

1. **Drop mirror CI entirely** (Go / OpenStack / LibreOffice / AOSP model). Zero red X's, zero
   cycles. Cost: loses the safety net unless a Gerrit-side post-merge job replaces it.
2. **Collapse instead of cancel** (Zuul supercedent semantics). GitHub cannot express this
   natively; closest is today's behavior plus run deletion. Hack by its own author's admission.
3. **Schedule-only main health run** (`on: schedule`, drop the `push` trigger for `main`).
   The ONLY option that removes cancellations by construction rather than hiding them. Surfaces
   as a workflow badge / Actions tab, not a per-commit mark - which matches the stated intent.
   Cost: attribution.  **← CHOSEN, at a 6-hour cadence.**
4. **Keep per-commit but make it cheap** (Qt model). Preserves attribution; costs cycles
   proportional to commit rate.

**The attribution cost, and how these projects pay it:** Chromium proves batching is survivable -
post-submit every 7-10 hours, accepting a multi-commit regression range, closed by AUTOMATED
bisection (Findit: median 14 min for compile failures, 24 min for swarmed gtest) plus a HUMAN on
sheriff rotation plus tree-closure to stop the bleeding. OpenStack pays it differently: the gate
pipeline is strong enough that post-merge breakage is rare, and `post` jobs are largely artifact
promotion rather than validation.

Because Gerrit's `Verified` gate already tests every patchset, a red scheduled run means one of:
a semantic conflict between two independently-verified changes, environmental/dependency drift,
or a flake. The commit window between last-green and red is small enough that
`git bisect run <the same CI script>` resolves it in log2(n) steps - typically 3-5 builds.

## What NOT to do, and why

- **delete-cancelled-runs**: makes the timeline LOOK right while destroying the record, and fails
  open - a genuine failure racing a delete is indistinguishable.
- **`cancel-in-progress: false` as a one-liner**: does not work (see mechanics above).
- **GitHub merge queue**: structurally inapplicable.
- **`queue: max`**: does produce all-green per-commit, but spends MORE cycles than today and
  directly contradicts the stated intent.

comments.body:
Implemented and pushed for review as Gerrit change 1437 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1437).

Dispositions, one per workflow that ran on a push to main:
- test.yml / optionality.yml / verify-identity.yml — main added to push.branches-ignore; 6-hourly schedules at minutes 41/47/53. Non-main push CI preserved.
- prompt-eval.yml — main added to push.branches-ignore; weekly live-tier cron untouched.
- codeql.yml — push key dropped entirely; weekly security scan kept; workflow_dispatch added (it had none).
- terraform-drift.yml — push key dropped entirely; daily drift sweep kept.
Untouched by instruction: gerrit-verify.yaml, both reconcilers, external-integration.yml, mirror-guard.yml, and all four workflow_call reusables — proven by the diff, which lists none of them.

test.yml also gains a caller-level main-health-report job (schedule/dispatch only, if: always()) that resolves the last known-green SHA from the Actions API and renders the bisect recipe. Both the lookup and the rendering live in scripts/main_health_report.py with the gh call injected as a Runner, so the failure modes are unit-tested. The job is added to check_verify_gate_parity.py EXCLUDED_JOBS and to the workflow-parity test's intentional-asymmetry set, because it gates nothing and has no Verified-lane counterpart.

Local gates green: make lint, make typecheck, make config-check, the Verified-gate parity script, and the full CI pytest invocation. One unrelated pre-existing local failure in tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py (grounding backend availability) is untouched by this change.

Plan-review attestation was earned only after working around ticket 895c-3eb2-043a-4de1: the Bedrock grammar-compilation failure on the standard model class. Running with REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL pointed at opus-4-8 let the verification pass complete, which then produced a real blocking finding (the actions: read + GH_TOKEN precondition for the run-history lookup) that four earlier INDETERMINATE runs had never surfaced.

# APPROVED BY THE OPERATOR — implement Option 3 (scheduled main-health CI, every 6 hours)

The research below is complete and the recommendation has been **approved**. Do not re-litigate
the approach; the operator's instruction and the constraints are recorded in
"Operator's decision" immediately below, and the acceptance criteria at the end are binding.

## Operator's decision (the thing to implement)

1. **GitHub CI for `main` runs on a SCHEDULE, not on push to `main`.** Cadence: **every 6 hours**
   — that is the signal density the operator wants. Use an **off-the-hour minute** (not `0`) so
   this repo's runs do not pile onto the hour boundary with every other project on the platform.
2. **Evaluate EVERY GitHub Actions workflow so the policy is CONSISTENT** — no workflow keeps a
   push-on-`main` trigger merely because nobody looked at it. Each workflow gets an explicit,
   recorded disposition.
3. **External-integration jobs stay at MOST once a day.** Their frequency must not increase.
   `external-integration.yml` is weekly today and stays weekly.
4. **Gerrit-verify and the reconciler workflows MUST NOT be changed** — they are separate
   mechanisms with their own semantics (`gerrit-verify.yaml`'s concurrency keys on
   `GERRIT_CHANGE_ID` as a deliberate stale-patchset guard; the reconcilers deliberately run
   with `cancel-in-progress: false`).
5. **`workflow_dispatch` must remain (or be added)** on every main-health workflow, so anyone can
   ask "is `main` healthy?" on demand without waiting for the tick.
6. **Pay for the loss of per-commit attribution, explicitly.** Two items from the approved
   recommendation are NOT optional:
   - Write the **`git bisect run` command into the workflow's FAILURE OUTPUT**, so remediation is
     one copy-paste. A scheduled run covers many commits; the first responder must not have to
     reconstruct the technique under pressure.
   - **Publish the last-known-green `main` SHA** so a bisect has a lower bound (Zuul's periodic
     pipelines and vLLM's "greenest commit on main" practice are the precedent).

## The confirmed mechanism (verify, do not re-derive)

`test.yml` declares:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

On `main`, `github.ref` is the constant `refs/heads/main`, so every push to `main` lands in ONE
concurrency group and cancels the previous run. Cancelled runs render as a red X on the commit
list, and GitHub offers no native way to suppress that (see mechanics below).

Note that the affected workflows filter pushes with `branches-ignore: ["feature/**"]`, which
**includes `main`** — so `main` must be added to that ignore list explicitly. Branch-push CI for
NON-`main` branches is preserved.

## Prior art and options analysis

The full research — what four of five major Gerrit-primary mirrors (golang/go, openstack/nova,
LibreOffice/core, aosp-mirror, qt/qtbase) surface on GitHub, where their real post-merge signal
lives (Go on LUCI; Zuul's supercedent `post` pipeline plus `periodic` pipelines; Chromium's
7-10-hourly post-submit backed by automated bisection and a sheriff rotation), the verified
GitHub Actions mechanics (cancelled == red X is unfixable natively; `cancel-in-progress: false`
does not help; a workflow cannot decline to report; merge queue is structurally inapplicable),
the four options considered, and the rejected alternatives (`delete-cancelled-runs`, `queue:
max`) — is recorded verbatim as a comment on this ticket. It is settled input to the approved
decision above, not open scope.

## Scope — the trigger inventory this change reasons over

Candidates (run on push to `main` today):

| Workflow | Trigger today | Cancels? |
|---|---|---|
| `test.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | yes (`test-${{ github.ref }}`) |
| `optionality.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | no |
| `verify-identity.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch | no |
| `prompt-eval.yml` | push `branches-ignore: [feature/**]` + PR + dispatch + weekly | yes |
| `codeql.yml` | push `branches: [main]` + weekly | yes |
| `terraform-drift.yml` | push `branches: [main]` path-filtered `infra/terraform/**` + daily + dispatch | no |

Out of scope, MUST NOT be modified: `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `reconcile-bridge.yml`,
`reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`, `external-integration.yml`, `mirror-guard.yml`, `lockdown.yml`,
`release.yml`, `jira-dc-*.yml`, `structured-output-baseline.yml`, and the four `workflow_call`
reusables (`_artifact-probe.yml`, `_build-and-test.yml`, `_eval-discipline.yml`,
`_optionality.yml`) — the reusables have no triggers of their own, so only their CALLERS change.

## The safety property that makes this acceptable

Pre-merge gating is **unchanged**. The Gerrit `Verified` lane runs the reusable
`_build-and-test.yml` (and `_artifact-probe.yml`) through `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s
`workflow_dispatch`, which is triggered by Gerrit per patchset. Editing `test.yml`'s **triggers**
cannot alter that lane, because the lane never reads `test.yml`. Every change still needs
`LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1` to land. The mirror's `main` CI is, and remains, a safety net —
the change only alters WHEN the safety net runs, never what gates a merge.

## Files this touches

`.github/workflows/test.yml`, `.github/workflows/optionality.yml`,
`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`, `.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml`,
`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml`, a new
`scripts/main_health_report.py` (the report renderer, kept out of the workflow YAML so the
suite can drive it), and two new test modules under `tests/unit/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No workflow triggers on a push to `refs/heads/main`.** For each of `test.yml`,
      `optionality.yml`, `verify-identity.yml`, `prompt-eval.yml`, `codeql.yml`, and
      `terraform-drift.yml`, a push event whose ref is `refs/heads/main` matches no trigger.
- [ ] **AC2 — The four `branches-ignore` workflows exclude `main` explicitly.** `test.yml`,
      `optionality.yml`, `verify-identity.yml`, and `prompt-eval.yml` list `main` alongside
      `feature/**` in `push.branches-ignore`.
- [ ] **AC3 — The two `branches: [main]` workflows drop their `push` key outright.**
      `codeql.yml` and `terraform-drift.yml` have no `push` trigger at all (each had only
      `branches: [main]`, so there is no other branch to preserve).
- [ ] **AC4 — Push CI for NON-`main` branches is preserved.** The four `branches-ignore`
      workflows still trigger on a push to a topic branch such as `wip-some-topic`.
- [ ] **AC5 — `feature/**` stays excluded.** The existing S3-replicated feature-branch
      exclusion is unchanged in all four `branches-ignore` workflows.
- [ ] **AC6 — The three cheap branch-health lanes gain a 6-hourly schedule.** `test.yml` gets
      `41 */6 * * *`, `optionality.yml` gets `47 */6 * * *`, `verify-identity.yml` gets
      `53 */6 * * *` — four "is main healthy" runs a day each, at deliberately staggered
      off-the-hour minutes so this repo's runs neither pile onto the hour boundary that every
      other project schedules onto nor onto each other.
- [ ] **AC7 — `prompt-eval.yml` keeps its weekly cron `0 7 * * 1` and gains no 6-hourly cron.**
      Its live tier is billable; 6-hourly would be a 28x cost increase nobody asked for.
- [ ] **AC8 — `codeql.yml` keeps its weekly cron `23 4 * * 1` and gains no 6-hourly cron.** A
      security scanner's cadence is a deliberate cost/coverage choice.
- [ ] **AC9 — `terraform-drift.yml` keeps its daily cron `17 6 * * *` and gains no 6-hourly
      cron.** The daily sweep is already this workflow's branch-health signal.
- [ ] **AC10 — Every one of the six workflows has `workflow_dispatch`**, so on-demand "is main
      healthy?" works without waiting for the tick (`codeql.yml` gains one; it had none).
- [ ] **AC11 — The last-known-green `main` SHA is resolved from the workflow's own successful
      run history** — `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/test.yml/runs` filtered by
      `status=success` and the current `branch`, newest first. No new state is persisted: the
      GitHub side is a read-only mirror, so nothing is pushed.
- [ ] **AC11a — That lookup's auth precondition is declared, not assumed.** The run-history
      endpoint needs BOTH the `actions: read` scope and a token on the step. The
      `main-health-report` job therefore declares `permissions: {contents: read, actions: read}`
      and the step passes `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. Missing either would 403, and the
      report would silently degrade to its AC14 placeholder on EVERY run instead of visibly
      once — a permanently useless lower bound is worse than an obviously absent one.
- [ ] **AC12 — A GREEN scheduled/dispatched run publishes its own SHA as the new last-known-green
      value** to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, so the lower bound is discoverable before an incident,
      not only during one.
- [ ] **AC13 — A RED scheduled/dispatched run publishes a copy-pasteable remediation recipe** to
      `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`: a `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` line with both SHAs filled
      in, followed by a `git bisect run` command using this repo's own CI reproduction
      (`uv sync --locked --extra dev`, then `make check`, then `make test`).
- [ ] **AC14 — Unresolvable last-known-green degrades gracefully.** Whenever the lower bound
      cannot be established — the Actions API returns no earlier successful run, OR the call
      itself fails (timeout, 4xx/5xx, rate limit, malformed body) — the report emits a recipe
      with a VISIBLE placeholder lower bound plus an explanation, and the step still exits 0. A
      missing lower bound must never turn a green `main` red, and a plausible-but-wrong SHA
      would send the bisect through commits that were never green.
- [ ] **AC15 — The report is emitted from a NEW caller-level job in `test.yml`, never from a
      reusable.** `test.yml`'s gates run inside `_build-and-test.yml` / `_artifact-probe.yml`,
      which are in the untouchable set and accept no caller steps; the report therefore lives in
      a caller-level `main-health-report` job with `if: always()` that `needs` every gating job.
      It is carried by `test.yml` only — that is the lane whose failure implies a code
      regression worth bisecting; `optionality.yml` and `verify-identity.yml` are single-purpose
      checks whose failure names its own cause.
- [ ] **AC16 — BOTH the lookup and the rendering live in a repo script, not inline YAML**, so
      they are unit-testable off a CI runner (workflow YAML is not reachable by the test
      suite). The `gh` call is injected as a `Runner` — the pattern `scripts/canary_bridge.py`
      already uses for its Actions-API reads — so every failure mode is exercised without a
      network, and the workflow keeps a single step rather than hand-rolled `jq` plumbing.
- [ ] **AC17 — The live external tier does not fire more often.** Dispatching `test.yml` is now
      the routine "is main healthy?" button, so its `external` job requires an explicit
      `run_external` dispatch input defaulting to false, and the schedule can never reach it.
- [ ] **AC18 — `external-integration.yml` is unmodified** and stays on its weekly
      `0 6 * * 1` cron, within the once-a-day cap.
- [ ] **AC19 — The separate mechanisms are byte-identical.** `git diff` shows no change to
      `gerrit-verify.yaml`, `reconcile-bridge.yml`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml`,
      `mirror-guard.yml`, or any `_*.yml` reusable.
- [ ] **AC20 — Automated regression coverage pins the trigger policy** — a test asserts, per
      workflow, that a push to `refs/heads/main` does not match, that non-`main` push CI
      survives, that each cadence is as specified, that dispatch is present, and that the
      untouchable set is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC21 — Automated coverage pins the report rendering** — tests assert the green path
      names the head SHA as the new lower bound, that an unproven (cancelled/skipped) gate is
      never reported as green, and that the red path emits a `git bisect start` line carrying
      both the bad and the resolved good SHA plus a balanced, single-quoted `git bisect run`
      command that reproduces CI.
- [ ] **AC21a — Automated coverage pins EVERY lookup failure mode**, not just empty history: a
      non-zero `gh` exit (403 from a missing scope, 5xx, rate limit, timeout), an empty run
      list, a malformed body, and an unexpected response shape each yield no bound rather than
      raising or inventing one — and the CLI still exits 0 in each case.
- [ ] **AC22 — Every touched workflow parses and lints.** `make lint` (which runs actionlint
      over every workflow), `make typecheck`, and `make test` are all green.
- [ ] **AC23 — The Verified-gate parity guard stays green.**
      `scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` fails the build when a job that gates `main` on a
      mirror lane is absent from `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `vote.needs`. The new
      `main-health-report` job is schedule/dispatch-only and never runs on the push/PR critical
      path, so it is added to that script's `EXCLUDED_JOBS` with a one-line justification —
      the documented escape hatch, alongside `external` and `eval-live`. `gerrit-verify.yaml`
      itself is NOT edited, so AC19 holds.
- [ ] **AC24 — The policy is written down outside this ticket.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 ("GitHub
      is a read-only mirror") gains a short subsection stating that mirror `main` CI is
      scheduled, why (cancelled runs render as red X on a healthy `main`), that pre-merge
      gating is unaffected, and how to respond to a red tick (dispatch to re-check; the run
      summary carries the bisect recipe and the last-known-green SHA).

## Verification

- `make lint` — includes actionlint over every workflow file (AC22).
- `make typecheck` and `make test` (AC22).
- `tests/unit/test_ci_main_push_policy.py` — the trigger-policy suite: AC1-AC10, AC15, AC17,
  AC18, AC19, AC20.
- `tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py` — the report-rendering suite driving the script
  directly with stubbed inputs: AC12, AC13, AC14, AC21.
- Recorded in the change itself: for each changed workflow, the resulting `on:` block and the
  explicit reason `refs/heads/main` no longer matches it (AC1).

## Explicitly NOT determined (do not treat as settled)

- Whether qt/qtbase sets a `concurrency` block - its all-green story is INFERRED from the trigger
  and speed comments, not confirmed.
- Whether OpenStack/Wikimedia `post` pipelines run VALIDATION or only artifact/doc publishing.
- Whether AOSP/Chromium mirrors deliberately suppress checks or simply have no workflows - the
  observable (0 check runs) was verified, the intent was not.
- Whether Findit still runs today and whether it auto-reverts.
- Kubernetes post-merge: verified only that Tide's docs do not cover it.
- GA status of the `queue:` concurrency option on the free/public Actions tier.

Drop push-on-main; add the 6-hourly branch-health schedule; refresh the CI-trigger audit comment.
Drop push-on-main; keep the weekly live-tier cadence unchanged.
Drop the push-on-main trigger; keep the weekly security-scan schedule; add workflow_dispatch.
Drop the push-on-main trigger; keep the daily drift sweep.

New: resolves the last-known-green SHA from the Actions API (gh injected as a Runner, the canary_bridge.py pattern) and renders the branch-health run summary — verdict, lower bound, bisect recipe, fail-soft degradation — as a repo script so it is unit-testable.
New regression test pinning the trigger policy: no main-push, preserved non-main push CI, the cadences, dispatch, the report job, and the untouched separate mechanisms.
New test driving the report renderer: green path, red path with a resolved lower bound, and the empty-history degradation path.

Record the mirror-CI policy in §3: main CI is scheduled, why, that pre-merge gating is unaffected, and how to respond to a red tick.
